summary: All six prescriptions are delivered in substance. The default view is genuinely quiet: header (back link, title, live state badge, pause/resume) → one refresh strip with scope + Run now → a four-cell status line with colour reserved for the two exceptions → three condensed run rows → a closed Settings drawer. Depth survives behind "Connection details", per-run disclosures, "More runs" and the single settings drawer, so the task path is short while configuration is clearly secondary. Type never drops below 0.875rem, controls hold 44px targets, the 1120px container keeps a sane measure at 1440, and the 390 view reflows to one column without overflow or truncation. Core controls and safety semantics are intact in source: pause/resume with edit preservation, run cancellation with cancel-requested state, version-conflict and auth-specific error copy, cron and cross-field validation with aria-invalid focus, dirty-state save/discard, and the drawer auto-opening on draft or validation state. Dark/gold identity and the handbook shell are unchanged. One visible inconsistency remains (badge title-casing); everything else I found is cosmetic and out of scope.
coverage_limits: Only the three supplied PNGs were inspected; I did not drive a browser and make no claim of interactive verification. User/browser verification remains parent-owned.

Conditional states (dirty settings, validation errors, active run with progress/cancel, paused collections, catalog failure/manual-ID fallback, loading and error banners) appear in no screenshot and were judged from source only.
Intermediate viewports between 390 and 1440 (notably the 601-850px band where the overview is two columns but settings are still two columns) were not pictured.
Contrast ratios, focus-visible rings, and token values from the global theme (var(--accent)/--warning/--muted) were not measured; those files were out of scope.
